extracted.intended_audience: ML researchers and dataset creators evaluating LLM mathematical reasoning and contest-style performance
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and evaluating multi-level mathematics benchmarks for large language models, including a structure-aware diagnostic set and a contest-style suite spanning educational stages and subjects, plus evaluation protocols and metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structure-aware diagnostic set (SKYLENAGE-ReasoningMATH)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 100-item, structure-aware diagnostic set designed to probe reasoning; items include per-item metadata.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper presents SKYLENAGE-ReasoningMATH as a 100-item diagnostic set that is 'structure-aware' and intended for fine-grained, reasoning-centered evaluation. It is explicitly sized (100 items) and paired with metadata to enable slice-based analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per-item metadata: length, numeric density, symbolic complexity
rubrics_metrics.description: Each diagnostic item contains metadata fields describing length, numeric density, and symbolic complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract lists these three metadata dimensions ('length, numeric density, and symbolic complexity') as part of the structure-aware diagnostic set; such metadata enable calibrated difficulty slices and analysis of model performance along concrete item attributes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest-style multi-stage suite (SKYLENAGE-MATH)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 150-item contest-style suite spanning four stages from high school to doctoral under a seven-subject taxonomy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SKYLENAGE-MATH is described as a contest-style evaluation with explicit staging (four stages corresponding to educational/competency levels) and a seven-subject taxonomy; the suite size is 150 items, intended to measure model performance across grade levels and subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seven-subject taxonomy
rubrics_metrics.description: Problems are organized under a seven-subject taxonomy to cover breadth of mathematical topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract emphasizes a seven-subject taxonomy for the contest suite, indicating that subject-level stratification is a design consideration and an axis for analysis (subject x model performance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-setup evaluation protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate multiple contemporary LLM variants under a single, consistent experimental setup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors evaluate fifteen contemporary LLM variants 'under a single setup' to ensure comparability; this implies standardized prompting, evaluation rules, and metrics across models to avoid confounding variability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-slice analysis: subject × model and grade × model
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze performance across dimensions by computing subject × model and grade × model performance matrices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper calls out explicit analyses of subject x model and grade x model performance, indicating that the benchmark should support per-subject and per-grade breakdowns to reveal where models succeed or fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary performance metric: accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Report percent-correct (accuracy) on benchmark suites as the main performance indicator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract reports accuracy values for models on the contest suite (e.g., strongest model reaches 44%) and on the reasoning set (best model attains 81%), implying accuracy is the primary aggregate metric for comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retention metric (doctoral-to-high-school retention)
rubrics_metrics.description: Define and report a retention ratio comparing performance at the highest stage (doctoral) to the lowest (high school), e.g., doctoral-to-high-school retention near 79%.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper uses a 'doctoral-to-high-school retention' statistic to quantify how well top systems maintain performance across difficulty levels; this is a designed metric to capture relative drop-off with increasing difficulty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardest-slice / robustness-gap analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate 'hardest-slice' performance to reveal robustness gaps between top models and mid-tier ones.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reasoning set's 'hardest-slice results' are used to highlight robustness gaps; the benchmark design and reporting should include slice-based hardest-case analyses to surface disparities not visible in overall accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calibrated difficulty and rich metadata as dataset design principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Construct benchmarks with calibrated difficulty levels and rich per-item metadata to support nuanced analysis and to avoid ceiling effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract motivates SKYLENAGE as 'a hard, reasoning-centered and broadly covering math benchmark with calibrated difficulty and rich metadata'—indicating design goals: (1) avoid ceiling effects, (2) enable diagnostic slicing, and (3) support broad coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dataset scale and explicit splits
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide explicit dataset scales and splits (e.g., 100-item diagnostic set vs. 150-item contest suite) to serve different evaluation purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors present two complementary sets (100-item diagnostic + 150-item contest-style) to serve distinct evaluation roles—fine-grained reasoning diagnosis vs. contest-style, multi-level assessment—suggesting a rubric to include both kinds of collections.
